thread:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing sustained KV residency growth on gpu-4 pools that lines up with longctx streams from tenant 'atlas'. pagewalks spiking and reuse is low. posting quick profile below and a couple of notes.

ashwin: link to the profile? perf-bot alerts? :eyes:

maria: pasted the 10m aggregate we pulled from the sampler: 
```
evictions/sec: 3.4 -> 9.8 (10m window)
avg_page_reuse_distance: 42k -> 170k
p99_kv_residency_per_tenant: 1.2GB -> 6.8GB
hot_pages_pct: 18% -> 6%
```

jordan: that looks less like simple growth and more like fragmentation + many single-touch pages. slab reuse low?

samir: I ran the fingerprint collector yesterday for atlas. here's the query I used to get candidates: 
```
SELECT tenant, fingerprint, touch_count FROM kv_page_stats WHERE window=10m ORDER BY touch_count DESC LIMIT 50;
```

lee: can you paste the fingerprint histogram? my hypothesis: longctx streaming creates lots of unique keys so reuse entropy is high -> eviction churn for co-tenants.

maria: histogram attached (summary): 70% of pages touched only once in window, top 1% fingerprints account for 40% of atlas touches but the long tail is huge. also noticed kernel selection skew: small-batch attention kernels used for these requests which increases per-request latency and causes more interleaved KV ops.

ashwin: mitigation ideas (brainstorm):
1) fingerprint-based soft quarantine: detect tenants with very high unique-page-rate and lower their KV residency watermark dynamically.
2) eviction priority tweak: prefer evicting fragmented holes and pages with low reuse entropy.
3) bump the fingerprint sampling frequency for tenants > X MB so we detect earlier.

jordan: experiments to validate:
A) soft-cap: reduce residency watermark by 20% for detected tenants and measure neighbor tail latency.
B) runtime quarantine lane: move heavy-entropy tenants into lower-priority lane with stricter caps.
C) adaptive batching: increase batch size for affected model families to reduce kernel-switch overhead and KV interleaving.

samir: quick repro command for people who want to simulate atlas: 
```
python tools/kv_fingerprint_replay.py --tenant atlas --duration 5m --rate 200
```

lee: results from short staging run?

samir: ran A on a staging shard for 30m: neighbor p95 latency improved ~12%, global eviction rate dropped ~40% for the shard, CPU overhead +~3% due to fingerprinting. we also saw overall memory growth stop vs control.

maria: sounds promising. question: prefer node-level quarantine (move tenant) or runtime soft cap first? my vote: soft cap + telemetry so we can iterate quickly without moving traffic.

ashwin: agree. I'll open a canary: implement fingerprint detector + soft-cap flag. will run on staging then small prod canary. plan: staging 6h -> prod 6h on 2 nodes -> expand.

perf-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-fingerprint-detector v0.1 -> staging at 2068724001 by ashwin :rocket:

jordan: make sure dashboards expose per-tenant residency, fingerprint entropy, unique_page_rate, and soft-cap state. also add an alert when detector flips for >3 nodes.

maria: if soft quarantine doesn't tame atlas, we'll escalate to quota enforcement and consider a tenancy migration to dedicated capacity.

ashwin: noted. I'll also add a quick doc with rollout steps and rollback.

lee: :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all — follow-up after the staging canary run.
